groups.title: NSF project: Future Proofing for Age-Related Changing Cognitive Abilities Using Smart Objects as Assistive Technologies
bullets: Designed and built an AI agent (Python, Flask, Gemini, Gmail and Google Calendar APIs) that infers everyday context from a user's email and calendar, answers questions by voice or text, and lets people set plain-language rules it applies to its inferences in real time.

Led a 7-participant, 14-session co-design study with people living with MCI or dementia as lead PhD researcher: developed the protocols, used the agent as a design probe for participant-authored privacy rules, ran one-on-one remote sessions (Zoom, FigJam), mentored an undergraduate researcher, and paired three semi-structured interviews per participant with a two-week diary study.

Analyzed the data with reflexive thematic analysis and proposed an adaptive-systems framework of four user-configurable modules (sensing, inference, assistance authority, output delivery), implemented as a Raspberry Pi leaving-home reminder system (Gemini, dlib face recognition, Google Calendar, weather, Flask).

groups.title: Research Assistant
bullets: Analyzed older adults' self-presentation on TikTok, combining engagement data for 15,000+ videos from 23 creators with a team-coded set of 1,227 videos from 11 creators.
Mentored four undergraduate and graduate students across research and prototyping projects, from study procedures and qualitative analysis to building working prototypes.

summary: Built and shipped web features for an early-stage startup, working with it through an Arizona State University program.
bullets: Turned Figma designs into responsive web applications in React and TypeScript, iterating with the design team from handoff to release.
Designed and integrated RESTful APIs to move data between user-facing features and the backend.
Built a HubSpot chatbot that automated customer engagement, cutting manual intervention by 40%.
Standardized 550+ templates with global variables, so one change updates everywhere and manual updates dropped by 80%.

summary: Radar perception and object tracking for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), the technology behind features like adaptive cruise control.
bullets: Implemented C++ multi-object tracking with a Kalman Filter, Interacting Multiple Model (IMM), and Probabilistic Data Association Filter (PDAF), improving vehicle tracking accuracy by 10%.
Improved ADAS object classification by 5% through MATLAB-based feature extraction and radar data analysis.
Identified and resolved a critical bug in which a truck was classified as two separate cars, raising classification accuracy by 15%.
Labeled and validated 5,000+ video frames against radar sensor outputs.
